postTitle: More Than Two Partners: Protecting Everyone
topic: The law offers one spouse slot, and every other partner is covered only by documents

assumptions.notes: No euro figures. From the post: in most countries marriage covers two people at a time, so automatic protections reach one partner; other partners rely on documents; joint tax treatment, partner visas and legal parenthood (two legal parents at most in most countries) are not extendable by any document. Family law differs by country.

bandStory.disclosure: Illustrative. Family law, tax and immigration rules differ by country. Not legal advice.

Only one pair in a household of three partners can usually marry. That choice decides who is protected.

beats.narration: Marriage activates legal protections for two people. In a larger household, one partner may receive them while the others do not.
beats.subtext: Automatic, by document, or not at all

beats.narration: Automatic, for the spouse: inheritance when there is no will, often a survivor pension, and medical decisions.
Every other partner depends on documents. A will naming each partner. Beneficiary forms with a percentage each. Healthcare proxies, with alternates in an agreed order.
And some things no document extends. Joint tax treatment. A partner visa. Legal parenthood, which most countries cap at two parents.
Common workarounds include insurance for an expected tax cost, assets held in deliberate names, and a residence status of each partner's own.
beats.subtext: Insurance, names, a status of their own

caption.instagram:
Three partners share a home. If one dies without a will, a partner may inherit nothing.

Marriage switches on protections automatically: inheritance with no will, often a survivor pension, medical decisions. In a household of three or more partners, one partner can hold that slot. Every other partner is covered only by what is written down: wills naming each partner, beneficiary forms with a percentage each, healthcare proxies with alternates in an agreed order. And some things no document extends, such as joint tax treatment, a partner visa and legal parenthood, so the plan works around them.

Three questions: who holds the slot and why, how is each other partner covered, and what needs a workaround?
